summary: No current entry is supplied for ǧlb. glossary_lookup search ǧləb returned no hit; the distinct ġlb entry means besiegen/overwhelm. Preserve ǧ versus ġ rather than merge roots on a loose consonant match.

The first passage contrasts divine sending and voluntary coming with being brought by sin. The second has an overt destination li ʕito. Together they support a provisional I bring/draw lexical entry; neither establishes coercion or a separate invite meaning.

Arabic contact is a reader hypothesis consistent with the written forms; this packet does not establish an etymological citation. Base Preterit and Infectum forms remain open, with only attested forms printed.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses rest on the Turoyo; any English quoted below is copied from that supplied translation.
Confirm the ǧ consonant and borrowed bring/draw interpretation against recordings or a native speaker, especially ǧləblalox versus ġlb.
Provide the singular Preterit and Infectum base forms and confirm the segmentation of ǧləblalox and kǧəlbutu.
Sin is an inanimate cause of someone’s arrival, while the church passage has human agents and a reciprocal object. This participant difference does not justify another sense.
